note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for a physically active woman with 2 weeks of right knee pain and clicking provoked by running and repetitive knee flexion/extension; no rest pain or instability; brief early swelling resolved with ice; single episode of right toe tingling post-run; plan includes activity modification, ongoing ice, NSAID therapy (stronger anti-inflammatory prescribed), physiotherapy referral, and conditional imaging if indicated.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Right knee pain with clicking during exercise; occasional tingling in right toes after running.
- Onset/duration: ~2 weeks ago.
- Course/progression: Pain begins after ~20 minutes of running (~2.5–3 miles); most recent run required stopping due to worsening pain. No pain at rest currently; clicking noted during gym ab exercises involving repeated knee flexion/extension. Initial mild swelling after early run resolved with ice; no persistent swelling.
- Location/character: Pain felt centrally in the right knee but may shift toward the right (lateral) aspect.
- Exacerbating factors: Running; repetitive knee flexion/extension (e.g., during ab workouts).
- Relieving factors: Rest; ice. PRN ibuprofen provides some relief (per patient).
- Associated symptoms: One episode of tingling in right toes after a run (resolved). Reports sock indentation after prolonged standing (minor dependent swelling by history). Denies persistent numbness, color/temperature change, calf pain.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No giving way, locking, or instability.
  - Full ability to fully flex and extend the knee.
  - No pain going up/down stairs; no pain with normal walking.
  - No current swelling, redness, or warmth.
  - No back pain or small joint pains/swelling.
- Activity context: Training for a marathon in June; running 4–5 miles with a couple of ~7-mile runs; increased running began ~1 month ago; also goes to gym several times per week. Prior fall while playing ice hockey months ago caused a bruise only; no immediate knee problems noted.
- Systems review: Denies GI symptoms, asthma, indigestion, acid reflux. No systemic illness or fever reported.

Past Medical History:
- Farsightedness; prior LASIK surgery.
- Prior severe urinary tract infection episode; evaluated in ER for suspected kidney stones.
- No other chronic conditions documented.

Social History:
- Highly active; training for a marathon; participates in sports including ice hockey.
- Lives in London.
- Substance use: Occasional cannabis use (“smoke a joint”).
- Smoking: Not documented.
- Alcohol: Not documented.
- Occupation/financial/lifestyle factors: Not documented.

Family History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented (telehealth).
- Patient-reported knee status at time of call:
  - Right knee: No current swelling; full active range of motion; no pain at rest; no locking or giving way.
  - Gait/functional: No pain with normal walking or stairs.

Investigations:
- None performed or reported.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Right knee pain with clicking, activity-related, likely overuse injury.
  - Assessment: Pattern and location consistent with iliotibial band friction syndrome (lateral knee overuse) vs patellofemoral pain syndrome; less likely meniscal pathology given no locking, instability, or discrete twisting injury. DDx supports ITBFS (high likelihood) and PFPS (moderate), meniscal pathology (low–moderate).
  - Plan:
    - Activity modification: Ease up on running; avoid running through pain. Stop activity if pain forces stopping.
    - Ice therapy: Continue frequent icing as previously used.
    - Medications: Stronger anti-inflammatory prescribed to take regularly with food; do not combine with ibuprofen (name/dose/route/frequency not documented). PRN ibuprofen otherwise acceptable when not taking the prescribed anti-inflammatory.
    - Referral: Physiotherapy referral placed for comprehensive knee assessment and management.
    - Imaging: Consider knee imaging if guided by in-person/physio exam to evaluate cartilage or other intra-articular pathology.
    - Red flags/return precautions: Seek urgent care if persistent swelling, heat, redness, high temperature, systemic unwellness, or if the knee locks/cannot bend/straighten.
    - Follow-up: If physiotherapy wait is long, option to be seen in clinic for examination.

- Issue 2: Transient right toe tingling after running.
  - Assessment: Single, self-limited episode with no ongoing neurologic deficits; DDx notes possible transient peripheral nerve irritation related to activity/footwear; not primary driver of knee pain.
  - Plan:
    - Monitor for recurrence, persistent numbness/weakness, color/temperature changes, or pain; seek care if these occur.

- Issue 3: NSAID use and safety.
  - Assessment: Patient uses ibuprofen 400 mg PRN; sometimes naproxen (Aleve). New stronger anti-inflammatory prescribed.
  - Plan:
    - Do not take multiple NSAIDs simultaneously (e.g., avoid combining ibuprofen and naproxen or the newly prescribed anti-inflammatory).
    - Take NSAIDs with food to reduce GI risk.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Iliotibial band friction syndrome (High): Lateral-leaning pain starting after several miles with recent mileage increase and clicking during flexion/extension; no locking/instability; full ROM.
- Patellofemoral pain syndrome (Moderate): Overuse/anterior knee mechanism with crepitus; provoked by running and repetitive flexion/extension; less classic given absence of stair pain and less clearly anterior localization.
- Meniscal pathology (Low–Moderate): Clicking and one episode of swelling could fit; less likely without locking, joint line tenderness, or clear twisting injury.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Allergies not documented; smoking and alcohol history not documented; comprehensive medication list with doses/routes/frequencies incomplete; vitals and physical exam not performed (telehealth); occupation and family history not documented.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Clear; occasional colloquial language; no major inaudible segments.
